# Spacesheep 🐑: Documents of the future

A new surface where people understand and work with AI.

Michael Makarov

Spacesheep

#consumer#productivity#generative\_ai#collaboration#developer\_tools

Hey everyone, I'm Michael, the founder of Spacesheep (F26).

## TL;DR

Spacesheep: documents of the future. Spaces are the place your teams and agents can be productive. Your AI makes the space; your team reads it, comments on it and builds on it.

Ask the AI you already use: "Use spacesheep.dev and give a visual explanation of how GPUs work." You get a document, a mockup, a dashboard, an app or art. Share it with specific people, your team, or publicly.

Our launch video: [...] ### Interactive designs

An interactive map of the ET-SoC-1 chip you can click through and comment on, from the whole chip down to a single vector unit. Each space is designed from scratch for what's in it. No templates.

### Apps, CRMs and forms

Teams build their own internal apps, CRMs and forms, even games: for productivity, for fun, or for working with suppliers and customers. Everyone edits the same records, and there are no servers to run.

### Collaborate

Jump on a space with your team and your AI. Comment on the exact line. Write @spacesheep and the AI fixes the space while everyone watches. Every version is kept.

This is how James Briggs uses it to stay in the loop while Claude Code writes his code: plans, code explainers and reviews he can actually read. [...] ### Never lose a link

Ask in your own words and the space is there. State-of-the-art search, built by former Pinecone engineers.

### Use your AI. Or ours.

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT, Grok and open-source harnesses like opencode all publish to the same space. Or use Spacesheep's own AI on the dashboard, in Slack and more.

### Own your data

Your spaces are yours. Every space and every version syncs to your own Google Drive or GitHub, so you can read them anywhere, take them with you, and never depend on us to keep them.

## About me

Founder/CEO of Spacesheep (YC F26). Previously MTS at Anthropic, where I built the internal app deployment framework and the first version of CC Artifacts. Before that, staff engineer at Pinecone and Twitter.
